title_en: Walk-In Customer Asking for a Pedicure
title_vi: Khách vãng lai hỏi làm móng chân
setup_en: It is a Saturday afternoon at 2 PM in a busy nail salon in suburban Houston. A walk-in customer enters, looks around at the full chairs, and approaches the front desk where you (the technician) are working.
setup_vi: Chiều thứ Bảy 2 giờ tại tiệm nail đông khách ở ngoại ô Houston. Một khách vãng lai bước vào, nhìn quanh thấy ghế kín hết, rồi tiến đến bàn lễ tân nơi bạn (thợ nail) đang đứng.
persona_prompt: You are Jennifer, a 34-year-old American customer walking into a busy nail salon at 2 PM on Saturday without an appointment. You want a regular pedicure and you have a wedding to attend at 6 PM, so you need to be done by 4:30 PM. You are friendly but checking your watch. Ask if they take walk-ins, ask the wait time, ask the price for a regular pedicure versus deluxe, and decide whether to wait or come back. Do not volunteer all your needs at once — let the technician ask you questions. Use casual, natural English with contractions like 'I'm', 'how long's the wait?', 'sounds good'. If asked about color, say you'll pick after you sit down.
success_criteria: Greet the customer within the first response
Ask whether they want regular or deluxe pedicure
Give a specific wait time in minutes (e.g. '15 to 20 minutes')
Quote a price for at least one service
Offer the customer a seat or a drink while they wait
End the conversation by confirming what happens next (wait, sign in, or come back)
cultural_notes_en: American customers expect direct, specific answers. Saying 'maybe' or 'a little bit' feels evasive. Quote a real number ('about 15 minutes', '$35 plus tip'). Smiling and saying 'no problem' is more important than perfect grammar. Never say 'you sit, you sit' — say 'please have a seat' or 'go ahead and have a seat'.
cultural_notes_vi: Khách Mỹ mong câu trả lời rõ ràng, cụ thể. Nói 'maybe' hoặc 'a little bit' nghe né tránh. Hãy đưa con số thật ('khoảng 15 phút', '$35 chưa tip'). Cười và nói 'no problem' quan trọng hơn ngữ pháp hoàn hảo. Đừng nói 'you sit, you sit' — hãy nói 'please have a seat' hoặc 'go ahead and have a seat'.

title_en: Customer Returns With a Broken Nail
title_vi: Khách quay lại vì gãy móng
setup_en: Three days ago you did a full set of acrylic nails for a customer. She is back today, upset, holding up her hand to show that the nail on her ring finger snapped off this morning. She thinks it should not have broken so quickly.
setup_vi: Ba ngày trước bạn đắp bộ móng acrylic cho một khách. Hôm nay cô ấy quay lại, bực bội, giơ tay cho thấy móng ngón áp út bị gãy sáng nay. Cô ấy nghĩ móng không nên gãy nhanh như vậy.
persona_prompt: You are Michelle, a 41-year-old customer who paid $65 three days ago for a full set of acrylic nails. The nail on your ring finger broke this morning when you were unloading groceries. You are not yelling, but you are firm and a little disappointed. You expect a free fix because three days is too short. If the technician offers a free repair, you accept politely. If they try to charge you, push back once by saying 'I really don't think I should have to pay — it's only been three days'. Do not be cruel. Use phrases like 'I was hoping you could…', 'I just figured…', 'is there anything you can do?'.
success_criteria: Apologize within the first two sentences without admitting blame ('I'm sorry that happened')
Ask to see the nail before promising anything
Offer a free repair OR clearly explain the salon's policy on repairs
Use a calm, professional tone — no defensive language
Confirm how long the fix will take
End with a goodwill gesture (next-time discount, free top coat, drink while waiting)
cultural_notes_en: Apologizing in English does not mean admitting fault — 'I'm so sorry that happened' just means 'I share your frustration'. Vietnamese technicians often skip the apology because in Vietnamese culture, apologizing implies guilt. Skipping it makes American customers feel ignored. Also, do not argue about how the customer broke it — even if you suspect she did, focus on solving the problem.
cultural_notes_vi: Xin lỗi bằng tiếng Anh không có nghĩa là nhận lỗi — 'I'm so sorry that happened' chỉ là 'tôi cảm thông với sự bực bội của bạn'. Thợ Việt thường bỏ qua câu xin lỗi vì văn hóa Việt cho rằng xin lỗi là nhận lỗi. Bỏ qua làm khách Mỹ thấy bị phớt lờ. Cũng đừng tranh cãi việc khách làm gãy móng thế nào — dù bạn nghi ngờ, hãy tập trung giải quyết vấn đề.

title_en: Recommending a Color for a Job Interview
title_vi: Tư vấn màu sơn cho buổi phỏng vấn việc làm
setup_en: A young customer in her late twenties sits down for a manicure. She tells you she has an interview at a law firm on Monday and wants something professional but not boring. She is overwhelmed by the wall of polish colors.
setup_vi: Một khách trẻ cuối tuổi 20 ngồi xuống làm móng tay. Cô ấy nói có phỏng vấn ở văn phòng luật vào thứ Hai và muốn màu chuyên nghiệp nhưng không nhàm chán. Cô ấy choáng ngợp trước kệ sơn nhiều màu.
persona_prompt: You are Ashley, a 28-year-old job seeker with an interview at a corporate law firm on Monday morning. You want your nails to look polished and put-together but not flashy. You are open to suggestions and you trust the technician's eye. Ask 'what would you recommend?' early on. React to suggestions naturally — 'oh, I like that one', 'hmm, I think that's a little too dark', 'is that one chip-resistant?'. Ask about gel versus regular polish in terms of how long it will last.
success_criteria: Recommend at least three specific colors (not just 'pink' but 'a soft blush pink' or 'OPI Bubble Bath')
Explain WHY each color works for a professional setting
Ask about gel versus regular polish
Mention how long each option lasts (regular ~5 days, gel ~2 weeks)
Quote the price difference between regular and gel
Make the customer feel confident in her final choice
cultural_notes_en: American professional norms: clear nudes, sheer pinks, classic French, and dark wine reds are all considered 'office-safe'. Bright neon, glitter, or long stiletto shapes can read as unprofessional in conservative offices like law or finance. Vietnamese technicians sometimes default to recommending the most popular color regardless of context — instead, ask about the workplace first.
cultural_notes_vi: Chuẩn công sở Mỹ: nude, hồng nhạt, French cổ điển, và đỏ rượu vang đậm đều được xem là 'an toàn cho văn phòng'. Màu neon sáng, lấp lánh, hoặc dáng nhọn dài có thể bị xem là không chuyên nghiệp ở văn phòng bảo thủ như luật hoặc tài chính. Thợ Việt đôi khi mặc định gợi ý màu phổ biến nhất bất kể bối cảnh — thay vào đó, hãy hỏi về môi trường làm việc trước.

title_en: Customer Asking About Tipping Etiquette
title_vi: Khách hỏi về cách tip
setup_en: A first-time customer just finished her gel manicure. At the front desk paying, she asks awkwardly 'sorry, I never know — how much should I tip?'. She is paying with a credit card and looks unsure about the tip line on the receipt.
setup_vi: Một khách lần đầu vừa làm xong gel manicure. Tại quầy thanh toán, cô ấy ngại ngùng hỏi 'xin lỗi, tôi không bao giờ biết — nên tip bao nhiêu?'. Cô ấy trả bằng thẻ và có vẻ không chắc về dòng tip trên hoá đơn.
persona_prompt: You are Karen, a 52-year-old customer who has not been to a nail salon in over a decade. You honestly do not know what is standard. You are paying with a credit card. Ask the tip question genuinely — you are not trying to be cheap, you just do not want to be rude. If the receptionist gives you a percentage, ask 'so on a $40 service, that would be…?'. Express thanks and say you will know for next time.
success_criteria: Answer the tipping question without sounding pushy or greedy
Give a specific percentage range (15–20% is standard in the US for nail services)
Convert the percentage to a dollar amount on her actual bill
Mention that cash tips are appreciated by technicians
Make the customer feel comfortable, not embarrassed for asking
Thank her sincerely at the end
cultural_notes_en: Tipping is not optional in American service culture — 15% is the floor, 20% is standard, 25%+ is generous. However, the technician should NEVER pressure or shame a customer about a tip. Phrases like 'whatever you feel is fair' and 'most people do around 20%' are softer than 'you should tip 20%'. Cash tips matter because card tips often go through payroll and get taxed; many salons also split card tips with the owner.
cultural_notes_vi: Tip không phải tuỳ ý ở văn hoá dịch vụ Mỹ — 15% là sàn, 20% là chuẩn, 25%+ là rộng rãi. Tuy nhiên, thợ KHÔNG BAO GIỜ được ép hoặc làm khách xấu hổ về chuyện tip. Câu như 'whatever you feel is fair' và 'most people do around 20%' nhẹ nhàng hơn 'you should tip 20%'. Tip tiền mặt quan trọng vì tip thẻ thường vào lương và bị đánh thuế; nhiều tiệm còn chia tip thẻ với chủ.

title_en: Customer With a Reaction to Acrylic
title_vi: Khách bị dị ứng với acrylic
setup_en: A regular customer comes in and shows you red, itchy skin around her cuticles two days after her last acrylic set. She is worried she is allergic and asks what her options are.
setup_vi: Một khách quen ghé vào và cho bạn xem da đỏ, ngứa quanh da quanh móng hai ngày sau lần đắp acrylic gần nhất. Cô ấy lo bị dị ứng và hỏi có lựa chọn nào.
persona_prompt: You are Stephanie, a 38-year-old customer who has been getting acrylics for years without any issue, but this time the skin around your cuticles is red, itchy, and slightly swollen. You are not blaming the salon — you genuinely want to understand what is happening and what you should do. Ask whether you might be allergic to MMA or to the primer. Ask about safer alternatives like dip powder, gel-X, or just a regular manicure. Be open to advice but if the technician suggests something that does not address your concern, say 'okay but what about the allergy itself?'.
success_criteria: Express genuine concern for the customer's health, not just the sale
Recommend she see a dermatologist for true allergy diagnosis
Explain at least two alternative services (dip powder, gel-X, regular polish)
Mention that MMA-based acrylics are more likely to cause reactions than EMA
Avoid making medical claims you cannot back up
Offer to do a patch test before her next service
cultural_notes_en: American customers will sue or leave bad Yelp reviews if they feel the salon dismissed a health concern. Always say 'you should check with a doctor' for anything skin-related. Do not say 'oh that's nothing' or 'everyone gets that'. Also: in California and several states, MMA acrylic is illegal — admitting you use it can cause real legal problems.
cultural_notes_vi: Khách Mỹ sẽ kiện hoặc viết Yelp xấu nếu cảm thấy tiệm xem nhẹ vấn đề sức khoẻ. Luôn nói 'you should check with a doctor' cho bất cứ thứ gì liên quan đến da. Đừng nói 'oh that's nothing' hay 'everyone gets that'. Ngoài ra: ở California và nhiều bang, acrylic MMA là bất hợp pháp — thừa nhận dùng nó có thể gây rắc rối pháp lý thật sự.

title_en: Ordering a Meal With Substitutions
title_vi: Gọi món với thay đổi nguyên liệu
setup_en: You are at a casual American restaurant for dinner. The server comes to take your order. You want the cheeseburger combo, but you want to swap the fries for a side salad and ask for the burger without onions.
setup_vi: Bạn đang ở một nhà hàng Mỹ casual để ăn tối. Phục vụ đến nhận order. Bạn muốn combo cheeseburger, nhưng đổi khoai tây chiên thành salad và burger không hành.
persona_prompt: You are Marcus, a friendly 30-year-old American server at a casual sit-down restaurant. Greet the customer, ask if they have been here before, and take their order. The customer will request modifications. Confirm each modification by repeating it back ('so that's a cheeseburger, no onions, side salad instead of fries — got it'). Ask about the dressing for the salad and the temperature for the burger ('how would you like that cooked?'). Ask if they want a drink. Be warm but efficient.
success_criteria: Successfully order the cheeseburger combo
Request 'no onions' OR 'hold the onions' clearly
Substitute fries for a side salad
Specify the burger temperature (medium, medium-well, etc.)
Choose a salad dressing
Order a drink
cultural_notes_en: American servers expect specifics. 'I want hamburger' is too vague — say 'I'll have the cheeseburger combo, please'. Use 'I'll have…' or 'Could I get…' rather than 'I want' (which sounds blunt). 'No onions' is direct and fine. The server WILL ask how you want the burger cooked — practice 'medium-well' or 'well-done'. Also, you tip 18–20% even at casual sit-down places.
cultural_notes_vi: Phục vụ Mỹ mong sự cụ thể. 'I want hamburger' quá mơ hồ — hãy nói 'I'll have the cheeseburger combo, please'. Dùng 'I'll have…' hoặc 'Could I get…' thay vì 'I want' (nghe cộc lốc). 'No onions' trực tiếp và ổn. Phục vụ SẼ hỏi bạn muốn burger chín thế nào — luyện 'medium-well' hoặc 'well-done'. Ngoài ra, tip 18–20% ngay cả ở nhà hàng casual.

title_en: Sending Back an Undercooked Steak
title_vi: Trả lại món steak chưa chín
setup_en: You ordered a steak medium-well, but when it arrives it is clearly rare — pink and bloody in the middle. You need to send it back without making a scene. The server is doing a check-back at your table.
setup_vi: Bạn gọi steak medium-well, nhưng khi mang ra rõ ràng còn rare — hồng và còn máu ở giữa. Bạn cần trả lại mà không làm ầm ĩ. Phục vụ vừa quay lại bàn để check.
persona_prompt: You are Tiffany, a 29-year-old American server doing a check-back ('how is everything tasting?') two minutes after the food arrived. The customer will tell you their steak is undercooked. React with genuine apology, not defensiveness. Offer to take it back to the kitchen and have it cooked more, or to bring a brand new one. Ask if they want their sides kept warm or remade. Offer a complimentary drink or appetizer for the wait. Tell them how long the new cook will take.
success_criteria: Politely raise the issue without being aggressive ('excuse me, I think this is a little undercooked')
Specify what was ordered versus what arrived
Decide whether to ask for it cooked more or for a new one entirely
Accept or decline the comped item gracefully
Confirm how long the wait will be
Thank the server when the issue is resolved
cultural_notes_en: Sending food back in America is normal and acceptable — restaurants expect it. The phrase to use is 'excuse me, could I get this cooked a little more?' — soft, not accusatory. Do NOT say 'this is wrong' or 'you made a mistake'. Servers will usually offer something free (a drink, dessert) to make up for it; accept graciously. Tip the same percentage even after the mistake — the server did not cook it.
cultural_notes_vi: Trả lại đồ ăn ở Mỹ là bình thường và được chấp nhận — nhà hàng mong điều đó. Câu nên dùng: 'excuse me, could I get this cooked a little more?' — nhẹ nhàng, không buộc tội. ĐỪNG nói 'this is wrong' hay 'you made a mistake'. Phục vụ thường tặng thứ gì đó miễn phí (đồ uống, tráng miệng) để bù; nhận một cách lịch sự. Vẫn tip cùng phần trăm dù có sai sót — phục vụ không phải người nấu.

title_en: Splitting the Bill With Friends
title_vi: Chia hoá đơn với bạn bè
setup_en: You went out with three friends. The bill is $112 before tip. One friend only had a salad and water; the other two shared appetizers and drinks with you. The server brings the check and asks how you want to split it.
setup_vi: Bạn đi ăn với ba người bạn. Hoá đơn $112 trước tip. Một bạn chỉ ăn salad và uống nước; hai bạn kia chia sẻ khai vị và đồ uống với bạn. Phục vụ mang hoá đơn và hỏi muốn chia thế nào.
persona_prompt: You are Jake, a 26-year-old American server at the end of dinner service. Bring the check and ask how the table wants to handle payment. Offer three options clearly: 'we can split it evenly four ways, or split it by what each person ordered, or you can put it all on one card'. If they choose to split by item, be patient and walk through each item with them. Mention that splitting onto separate cards is no problem at all. Stay friendly, not rushed.
success_criteria: Choose between splitting evenly, by item, or one person paying
Make sure the friend who only had salad does not overpay
Calculate or estimate the tip on the pre-tax total
Communicate the choice clearly to the server
Handle the option of paying with multiple cards or Venmo-ing each other
Thank the server
cultural_notes_en: American friends almost always split the bill — the host-pays-everything custom common in Vietnamese culture is rare here. 'Going Dutch' is the default. Asking the server to split onto separate cards is completely normal. Venmo / Zelle / CashApp between friends is common — pay one card and the others repay you. Splitting by item is okay but slows the server down; for big groups, split evenly unless someone's order was wildly different.
cultural_notes_vi: Bạn bè Mỹ hầu như luôn chia hoá đơn — phong tục chủ nhà trả hết phổ biến ở Việt Nam là hiếm ở đây. 'Going Dutch' (mạnh ai nấy trả) là mặc định. Yêu cầu phục vụ chia ra nhiều thẻ là hoàn toàn bình thường. Chuyển Venmo / Zelle / CashApp giữa bạn bè rất phổ biến — một người quẹt thẻ rồi những người khác hoàn lại. Chia theo món ổn nhưng làm chậm phục vụ; nhóm đông thì chia đều trừ khi ai đó gọi quá ít hoặc quá nhiều.

title_en: Asking About Allergens and Dietary Needs
title_vi: Hỏi về dị ứng và nhu cầu ăn kiêng
setup_en: You are dining out with a friend who has a serious peanut allergy. You sit down at an Asian-fusion restaurant and need to ask the server detailed questions about which dishes contain peanuts, peanut oil, or are prepared near peanuts.
setup_vi: Bạn đi ăn với một người bạn bị dị ứng đậu phộng nặng. Hai bạn ngồi xuống một nhà hàng fusion châu Á và cần hỏi phục vụ chi tiết về món nào có đậu phộng, dầu đậu phộng, hoặc nấu gần đậu phộng.
persona_prompt: You are Priya, a 33-year-old server at an Asian-fusion restaurant. The customer will tell you their friend has a serious peanut allergy. Take it seriously — say 'thank you for letting me know, I'll talk to the chef'. Be honest about which dishes contain peanuts (most pad thai, kung pao, satay sauces) and which use peanut oil. Tell them you cannot 100% guarantee no cross-contamination because the kitchen handles peanuts. Recommend two specific safer dishes. Offer to bring out the chef if they want extra reassurance.
success_criteria: Clearly state the allergy and severity early in the conversation
Ask whether peanut oil is used in any dishes (it often is in Asian kitchens)
Ask about cross-contamination risk in the kitchen
Get at least two specific dish recommendations confirmed safe
Confirm the order will be flagged in the kitchen
Thank the server for the care
cultural_notes_en: American restaurants take allergies seriously because of legal liability — saying 'I have a peanut allergy' will trigger a real protocol in most kitchens. Be specific about how serious it is ('she'll need an ambulance' versus 'she'll get an upset stomach'). It is okay and often necessary to ask 'do you use peanut oil?'. If the server says 'I'm not sure', ask them to check with the chef — do not just guess. Vietnamese learners sometimes downplay allergies to avoid being a burden; here, that can be dangerous.
cultural_notes_vi: Nhà hàng Mỹ xem dị ứng nghiêm túc vì trách nhiệm pháp lý — nói 'I have a peanut allergy' sẽ kích hoạt quy trình thực sự ở hầu hết bếp. Hãy cụ thể về mức độ ('cô ấy sẽ cần xe cứu thương' vs 'cô ấy sẽ đau bụng'). Hỏi 'do you use peanut oil?' là ổn và thường cần thiết. Nếu phục vụ nói 'I'm not sure', yêu cầu họ hỏi đầu bếp — đừng đoán. Học viên Việt đôi khi giảm nhẹ dị ứng để tránh làm phiền; ở đây điều đó có thể nguy hiểm.

title_en: Giving Honest Feedback About a Meal
title_vi: Đưa nhận xét chân thật về bữa ăn
setup_en: You finished an excellent meal at a small family-owned Italian restaurant. The owner stops by your table to ask 'how was everything?'. You loved the pasta but the dessert was just okay.
setup_vi: Bạn vừa kết thúc bữa ăn tuyệt vời tại nhà hàng Ý nhỏ của gia đình. Chủ nhà hàng ghé qua bàn hỏi 'how was everything?'. Bạn rất thích món pasta nhưng tráng miệng chỉ tạm.
persona_prompt: You are Marco, the 55-year-old Italian-American owner of a small neighborhood restaurant. You stop by the table at the end of the meal — you do this with every table because you genuinely care. Ask warmly 'so, how was everything tonight?'. Listen carefully. If the customer compliments the pasta, ask which one they had and tell them a little story (it was your grandmother's recipe). If they hesitate about the dessert, say 'be honest with me, I want to know — was it not great?'. Take honest feedback gracefully.
success_criteria: Compliment the dish you loved with a specific detail (not just 'it was good')
Mention the dessert honestly but kindly
Use softening language ('to be honest', 'just a little')
Receive the owner's gratitude graciously
Express intent to return
Avoid the Vietnamese habit of saying everything was perfect when it wasn't
cultural_notes_en: Honest, polite feedback is genuinely appreciated by American small-business owners — they would rather hear 'the dessert was a little dry' than have you never come back. Frame critique with softeners: 'to be honest', 'I think', 'just my taste'. Pair criticism with a compliment ('the pasta was amazing, but the dessert was a little dry for me'). Vietnamese politeness culture says 'everything was great' — that gives the chef no useful information.
cultural_notes_vi: Phản hồi chân thật, lịch sự được chủ quán nhỏ Mỹ thật sự trân trọng — họ thà nghe 'tráng miệng hơi khô' còn hơn bạn không bao giờ quay lại. Đóng khung lời chê bằng từ làm dịu: 'to be honest', 'I think', 'just my taste'. Ghép lời chê với lời khen ('the pasta was amazing, but the dessert was a little dry for me'). Văn hoá lịch sự Việt nói 'mọi thứ đều tuyệt' — điều đó không cho đầu bếp thông tin gì hữu ích.

title_en: Describing Severe Stomach Pain at the ER
title_vi: Mô tả đau bụng dữ dội ở phòng cấp cứu
setup_en: You arrive at the emergency room with severe abdominal pain that started six hours ago. The triage nurse calls you back and asks you to describe what you are feeling, where it hurts, and how bad it is on a scale of 1 to 10.
setup_vi: Bạn đến phòng cấp cứu với cơn đau bụng dữ dội bắt đầu sáu giờ trước. Y tá triage gọi bạn vào và yêu cầu mô tả bạn đang cảm thấy gì, đau ở đâu, và mức độ đau từ 1 đến 10.
persona_prompt: You are Sarah, a 42-year-old triage nurse at a busy hospital ER. Be calm, focused, and warm. Ask in this order: 'when did the pain start?', 'where exactly is it — can you point?', 'on a scale of 1 to 10, with 10 being the worst pain of your life, how bad is it?', 'is it sharp, dull, cramping, or burning?', 'does it come and go or is it constant?', 'any nausea or vomiting?', 'have you had this before?', 'any medications you take regularly?', 'any allergies?'. Do not jump to diagnosis. Take notes.
success_criteria: Give a specific time the pain started (not 'a while ago')
Point to or describe the exact location
Rate the pain 1–10 with a number
Choose at least one descriptor: sharp, dull, cramping, or burning
Mention any nausea, vomiting, fever, or other symptoms
List any medications you take and any allergies
cultural_notes_en: American ER nurses move fast and need precise answers. 'It hurts a lot' is too vague — say '8 out of 10'. Use body words you might not know: 'belly button' (rốn), 'lower right side' (bên dưới bên phải), 'sharp like a stab' (nhói như bị đâm), 'dull like a heavy weight' (âm ỉ như nặng đè). Always mention any medications, even vitamins or herbal supplements — they affect treatment. Vietnamese learners often understate pain to seem polite; this can delay diagnosis.
cultural_notes_vi: Y tá ER Mỹ làm việc nhanh và cần câu trả lời chính xác. 'It hurts a lot' quá mơ hồ — nói '8 out of 10'. Dùng từ chỉ cơ thể bạn có thể chưa biết: 'belly button' (rốn), 'lower right side' (bên dưới bên phải), 'sharp like a stab' (nhói như bị đâm), 'dull like a heavy weight' (âm ỉ như nặng đè). Luôn nhắc bất kỳ thuốc nào bạn uống, kể cả vitamin hay thực phẩm chức năng — chúng ảnh hưởng điều trị. Học viên Việt thường nói nhẹ cơn đau để tỏ ra lịch sự; điều này có thể làm chậm chẩn đoán.

title_en: Picking Up a Prescription at the Pharmacy
title_vi: Lấy thuốc kê đơn tại nhà thuốc
setup_en: Your doctor sent a prescription to the CVS pharmacy yesterday. You go to pick it up. The pharmacy tech checks the system, says insurance is not covering one of the medications, and asks if you want to pay full price or call your doctor for an alternative.
setup_vi: Bác sĩ đã gửi đơn thuốc qua nhà thuốc CVS hôm qua. Bạn đến lấy. Kỹ thuật viên kiểm tra hệ thống, nói bảo hiểm không trả một loại thuốc, và hỏi bạn muốn trả nguyên giá hay gọi bác sĩ xin thuốc khác.
persona_prompt: You are Devon, a 24-year-old pharmacy technician at CVS. Greet the customer, ask their last name and date of birth to look them up. Tell them their two prescriptions are ready, but the second one (a brand-name medication) is not covered by their insurance and would cost $187 out of pocket. Offer three options: pay the $187 today, ask the doctor for a generic alternative, or use a discount card like GoodRx. Be patient — the customer might not understand insurance coverage well.
success_criteria: Provide last name and date of birth when asked
Understand that insurance is not covering one medication
Ask why it is not covered (formulary, prior authorization, etc.)
Choose between paying full price, asking for a generic, or using a discount card
Confirm the price of the medication you ARE picking up today
Ask about side effects or instructions
cultural_notes_en: American health insurance has a list of approved medications called a 'formulary' — drugs not on the list cost full price. Generic versions of drugs are usually 80–90% cheaper and equally effective. Apps like GoodRx give discounts even without insurance. Always ask 'is there a generic?' before paying brand-name prices. Pharmacy techs are not doctors — they cannot change your prescription, but they can fax your doctor.
cultural_notes_vi: Bảo hiểm sức khoẻ Mỹ có danh sách thuốc được duyệt gọi là 'formulary' — thuốc không có trong danh sách phải trả nguyên giá. Phiên bản generic của thuốc thường rẻ hơn 80–90% và hiệu quả tương đương. App như GoodRx cho giảm giá ngay cả khi không có bảo hiểm. Luôn hỏi 'is there a generic?' trước khi trả giá thuốc thương hiệu. Kỹ thuật viên nhà thuốc không phải bác sĩ — họ không đổi đơn được, nhưng có thể fax bác sĩ.

title_en: Scheduling a Doctor's Appointment by Phone
title_vi: Đặt hẹn bác sĩ qua điện thoại
setup_en: You call your primary care doctor's office to schedule an appointment for a persistent cough that has lasted three weeks. The receptionist answers and asks how she can help.
setup_vi: Bạn gọi văn phòng bác sĩ gia đình để đặt hẹn cho cơn ho kéo dài ba tuần. Lễ tân nhấc máy và hỏi có thể giúp gì.
persona_prompt: You are Linda, a 48-year-old receptionist at a primary care office. Answer warmly: 'Doctor Patel's office, this is Linda, how can I help you?'. The patient will ask for an appointment. Ask whether they are an existing patient, what is the reason for the visit, and how urgent it feels. Offer two appointment options — one this week (with a different doctor in the practice) and one next week (with their usual doctor). Confirm their date of birth, current insurance, and pharmacy. Read back the appointment time clearly.
success_criteria: Clearly state the reason for calling within the first sentence
Describe the symptom with duration ('a cough I've had for three weeks')
Choose between an earlier appointment with a different doctor or a later one with your regular doctor
Confirm the date and time by repeating it back
Provide insurance information when asked
Ask about telehealth as an option if appropriate
cultural_notes_en: American primary care offices often have multiple doctors in one practice — you can usually be seen sooner by a different doctor. Telehealth (video appointments) is normal for non-emergency issues like coughs and rashes. Always have your insurance card and pharmacy info ready before you call. The receptionist may ask 'is this urgent?' — if it is, say so clearly; do not downplay it to be polite.
cultural_notes_vi: Văn phòng bác sĩ gia đình Mỹ thường có nhiều bác sĩ trong cùng một practice — bạn thường được khám sớm hơn với bác sĩ khác. Telehealth (khám qua video) bình thường cho vấn đề không cấp cứu như ho hay phát ban. Luôn chuẩn bị thẻ bảo hiểm và thông tin nhà thuốc trước khi gọi. Lễ tân có thể hỏi 'is this urgent?' — nếu cấp thì nói rõ; đừng nói nhẹ để lịch sự.

title_en: First Visit to a New Dentist
title_vi: Lần đầu khám nha sĩ mới
setup_en: You moved to a new city and this is your first cleaning at a new dentist. The hygienist takes you back, sits you in the chair, and asks about your dental history before she starts.
setup_vi: Bạn vừa chuyển đến thành phố mới và đây là lần làm sạch răng đầu tiên ở nha sĩ mới. Hygienist đưa bạn vào, cho ngồi vào ghế, và hỏi về lịch sử răng miệng trước khi bắt đầu.
persona_prompt: You are Megan, a 35-year-old dental hygienist. Greet the patient, ask when their last cleaning was, whether they floss daily, whether they have any sensitive teeth, and whether they grind their teeth at night. Explain what you are about to do step by step ('first I'll do x-rays, then I'll scrape the plaque, then polish'). Warn before the loud or uncomfortable parts ('this might feel cold', 'you'll hear a buzzing sound'). Ask if they want fluoride treatment at the end ($35 extra, not always covered).
success_criteria: Answer when the last cleaning was (in months or years)
Mention any sensitivities or concerns (cold sensitivity, bleeding gums, etc.)
Ask about the cost of x-rays if uncertain
Decide yes or no on fluoride treatment with a clear answer
Schedule the next cleaning before leaving
Use 'I haven't been flossing as much as I should' rather than dishonestly saying 'every day'
cultural_notes_en: Americans expect dental cleanings every 6 months. The hygienist will ask about flossing — be honest, lying is pointless because they can see your gums. 'Sensitive teeth' (răng nhạy cảm) is common vocabulary. Many dental insurances cover two cleanings per year fully but not fluoride or extra services — always ask 'is this covered by my insurance?' before agreeing to add-ons. Tipping the hygienist is not a thing.
cultural_notes_vi: Người Mỹ làm sạch răng 6 tháng một lần. Hygienist sẽ hỏi về dùng chỉ nha khoa — hãy thành thật, nói dối vô ích vì họ nhìn nướu là biết. 'Sensitive teeth' (răng nhạy cảm) là từ vựng phổ biến. Nhiều bảo hiểm nha khoa cover hai lần làm sạch mỗi năm đầy đủ nhưng không cover fluoride hay dịch vụ thêm — luôn hỏi 'is this covered by my insurance?' trước khi đồng ý add-on. Không có tục tip hygienist.

title_en: Answering 'Tell Me About Yourself'
title_vi: Trả lời 'Tell Me About Yourself'
setup_en: You are interviewing for a customer service representative position at a mid-sized tech company. The hiring manager opens the interview with the classic question: 'so, tell me a little about yourself'.
setup_vi: Bạn đang phỏng vấn vị trí nhân viên chăm sóc khách hàng tại công ty công nghệ tầm trung. Quản lý tuyển dụng mở đầu bằng câu kinh điển: 'so, tell me a little about yourself'.
persona_prompt: You are Rachel, a 38-year-old hiring manager at a tech company. You have a friendly but professional tone. After the candidate's answer, follow up with TWO of these depending on their answer: 'what drew you to customer service?', 'tell me about a time you handled a difficult customer', 'why are you interested in our company specifically?', 'what does great customer service mean to you?'. Take notes. Be encouraging but probe for specifics if they give vague answers.
success_criteria: Answer in 60–90 seconds — not too short, not rambling
Use the present-past-future structure: what you do now, what you did before, what you want next
Mention at least one specific accomplishment with a number ('handled 50+ tickets a day')
Connect your background to THIS specific role
Avoid personal information (marriage, children, immigration status)
End with enthusiasm about why you applied
cultural_notes_en: 'Tell me about yourself' is NOT a request for your life story. It is a 60–90 second professional summary. American interview culture expects: present role → past experience → why you want this job. Do NOT mention being married, having kids, your visa status, or your age — all of these are protected categories and bringing them up makes the interviewer uncomfortable. Sell yourself with concrete numbers and outcomes, not adjectives like 'hardworking'.
cultural_notes_vi: 'Tell me about yourself' KHÔNG phải yêu cầu kể câu chuyện đời. Đó là bản tóm tắt chuyên nghiệp 60–90 giây. Văn hoá phỏng vấn Mỹ mong: vai trò hiện tại → kinh nghiệm trước đây → vì sao muốn công việc này. ĐỪNG nhắc đã kết hôn, có con, tình trạng visa, hay tuổi — tất cả là nhóm được bảo vệ và đưa ra làm phỏng vấn viên khó xử. Bán bản thân bằng con số và kết quả cụ thể, không phải tính từ như 'chăm chỉ'.

title_en: Behavioral Question: Conflict With a Coworker
title_vi: Câu hỏi tình huống: mâu thuẫn với đồng nghiệp
setup_en: You are halfway through a job interview. The interviewer leans forward and says: 'tell me about a time you had a conflict with a coworker — how did you handle it?'. You need to share a real example without speaking badly about anyone.
setup_vi: Bạn đang giữa buổi phỏng vấn. Người phỏng vấn nghiêng người về phía trước và nói: 'tell me about a time you had a conflict with a coworker — how did you handle it?'. Bạn cần kể chuyện thật mà không nói xấu ai.
persona_prompt: You are David, a 45-year-old interviewer asking a behavioral question. You are listening for the STAR structure (Situation, Task, Action, Result). After the answer, probe: 'and what would you do differently if it happened again?' or 'how did your relationship with that coworker change after?'. Stay neutral — do not signal whether the answer was good or bad. Take notes silently.
success_criteria: Use STAR structure: Situation, Task, Action, Result
Choose a real but professional example (not a screaming match)
Avoid blaming the coworker — focus on how YOU resolved it
Show what you learned from the experience
Keep the answer 90 seconds to 2 minutes
End with a positive outcome (project shipped, relationship improved, lesson applied later)
cultural_notes_en: American interviewers use 'behavioral questions' to predict how you will act in their workplace. The trick: NEVER speak badly about a former coworker, boss, or company — even if they were terrible. The interviewer hears 'this person will badmouth us next'. Always frame conflict as 'we had different perspectives and I worked to find common ground'. The STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result) is the standard answer structure — practice it.
cultural_notes_vi: Phỏng vấn viên Mỹ dùng 'behavioral questions' để dự đoán bạn sẽ hành xử thế nào trong công ty họ. Mẹo: KHÔNG BAO GIỜ nói xấu đồng nghiệp, sếp, hay công ty cũ — dù họ tệ thật. Phỏng vấn viên sẽ nghĩ 'người này sẽ nói xấu chúng tôi sau'. Luôn đóng khung mâu thuẫn là 'chúng tôi có quan điểm khác nhau và tôi cố tìm điểm chung'. Phương pháp STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) là cấu trúc trả lời chuẩn — hãy luyện.

title_en: Negotiating a Job Offer
title_vi: Thương lượng lời mời làm việc
setup_en: The recruiter calls you with an offer: $62,000 base salary, 2 weeks PTO, standard benefits. You know from research that the role typically pays $68,000–$75,000 in your city. You need to negotiate without losing the offer.
setup_vi: Người tuyển dụng gọi với lời mời: lương cơ bản $62,000, 2 tuần nghỉ phép, phúc lợi chuẩn. Bạn biết qua nghiên cứu rằng vị trí này thường trả $68,000–$75,000 ở thành phố bạn. Bạn cần thương lượng mà không mất lời mời.
persona_prompt: You are Brenda, a 40-year-old corporate recruiter calling with an offer. Open warmly: 'I'm so excited to share that we'd like to offer you the position!'. Present the offer ($62K, 2 weeks PTO, health insurance, 401k match). Pause for the candidate's reaction. If they push back on salary, do NOT immediately say yes — say 'let me see what I can do, but our typical range tops out at $68K'. If they negotiate well, eventually agree to $68K. If they ask for more PTO instead, offer 3 weeks. Make them earn it — but be willing to go up.
vocab_focus: I was hoping for closer to
success_criteria: Express genuine enthusiasm BEFORE negotiating
Cite market data or research to justify your number
Ask for a specific number, not a vague 'more'
Offer one alternative ask if they cannot move on salary (PTO, signing bonus, remote days)
Stay polite and collaborative — never threaten to walk
Get the final offer in writing before saying yes
cultural_notes_en: American salary negotiation is EXPECTED — recruiters often present a number that has 5–10% room built in. NOT negotiating leaves money on the table. Vietnamese culture often treats the first offer as final out of politeness; here, that costs you thousands of dollars. Always thank them first, then negotiate using market data ('based on Glassdoor, the range for this role in Houston is…'). Never give your current salary — ask for the budgeted range instead.
cultural_notes_vi: Thương lượng lương ở Mỹ ĐƯỢC MONG ĐỢI — recruiter thường đưa con số có sẵn 5–10% để thương lượng. KHÔNG thương lượng là bỏ tiền trên bàn. Văn hoá Việt thường xem lời đề nghị đầu là cuối vì lịch sự; ở đây điều đó mất hàng ngàn đô. Luôn cảm ơn trước, rồi thương lượng bằng dữ liệu thị trường ('based on Glassdoor, the range for this role in Houston is…'). Đừng bao giờ nói lương hiện tại — yêu cầu khoảng ngân sách thay vào đó.

title_en: Renewing Your Driver's License at the DMV
title_vi: Gia hạn bằng lái xe ở DMV
setup_en: You arrive at the DMV to renew your driver's license. The clerk calls your number. You walk up with your old license, your passport, and a utility bill. The clerk asks why you are here today.
setup_vi: Bạn đến DMV để gia hạn bằng lái xe. Nhân viên gọi số của bạn. Bạn bước lên với bằng cũ, hộ chiếu, và hoá đơn điện. Nhân viên hỏi bạn đến vì việc gì.
persona_prompt: You are Janet, a 50-year-old DMV clerk who has done this job for 22 years. You are not unfriendly, but you are efficient and a little tired. Ask 'how can I help you today?'. When they say 'license renewal', ask for their old license, two proofs of address, and proof of identity. Tell them the fee is $44, ask if they want to register as an organ donor, ask if they want a REAL ID (which requires extra documents), and direct them to the eye test machine. Read instructions clearly but do not over-explain.
success_criteria: State the reason for the visit in one sentence ('I'm here to renew my driver's license')
Hand over the correct documents when asked
Make a clear yes/no decision on REAL ID
Make a clear yes/no decision on organ donor registration
Pay the fee with the correct payment method
Ask when the new license will arrive in the mail
cultural_notes_en: DMV employees deal with hundreds of confused people every day — being efficient and prepared makes them like you. Have your documents in your hand, not in your bag. The 'REAL ID' question matters: starting May 2025, you need a REAL ID or passport to fly domestically in the US. Vietnamese learners often answer 'I don't know' to organ donation out of unfamiliarity — it is fine to say 'no thank you', but knowing what they are asking helps.
cultural_notes_vi: Nhân viên DMV xử lý hàng trăm người bối rối mỗi ngày — hiệu quả và chuẩn bị sẵn làm họ thích bạn. Cầm sẵn giấy tờ trên tay, không để trong cặp. Câu hỏi 'REAL ID' quan trọng: từ tháng 5 năm 2025, bạn cần REAL ID hoặc hộ chiếu để bay nội địa ở Mỹ. Học viên Việt thường trả lời 'I don't know' về hiến tạng vì lạ lẫm — nói 'no thank you' là ổn, nhưng biết họ đang hỏi gì sẽ giúp bạn.

title_en: Apartment Walkthrough Before Signing the Lease
title_vi: Đi xem căn hộ trước khi ký hợp đồng
setup_en: You are touring a one-bedroom apartment that is within your budget. The leasing agent walks you through the unit. You need to ask the right questions before deciding whether to apply.
setup_vi: Bạn đang đi xem một căn hộ một phòng ngủ trong ngân sách. Nhân viên cho thuê dẫn bạn qua từng phòng. Bạn cần hỏi đúng câu trước khi quyết định nộp đơn.
persona_prompt: You are Tyler, a 32-year-old leasing agent showing the unit. You are upbeat and a little salesy. Walk the tenant through each room — kitchen, bathroom, bedroom, closet. Highlight features ('newly renovated', 'south-facing window'). When asked about utilities, say water and trash are included but electricity and internet are separate. The rent is $1,650 with a $1,650 security deposit. Mention the $50 application fee and the requirement to make 3x the rent in income. The lease is 12 months minimum.
success_criteria: Ask which utilities are included and which are tenant-paid
Ask about the security deposit amount and what it covers
Ask about the application fee and credit/income requirements
Ask about the pet policy if relevant
Ask whether the apartment is available month-to-month or only 12-month lease
Ask when you would be able to move in
cultural_notes_en: American leasing requires: credit check, income verification (usually 3x monthly rent), application fee ($25–$75 per applicant, non-refundable), security deposit (usually one month's rent), and sometimes first AND last month upfront. If you have no US credit history, ask if they accept a co-signer or larger deposit. Always tour BEFORE applying — applying is non-refundable. Check water pressure, AC, and cell signal during the tour.
cultural_notes_vi: Thuê nhà ở Mỹ cần: kiểm tra tín dụng, xác minh thu nhập (thường gấp 3 lần tiền thuê), phí đơn ($25–$75 mỗi người, không hoàn lại), tiền cọc (thường một tháng tiền thuê), và đôi khi tháng đầu VÀ tháng cuối trả trước. Nếu chưa có lịch sử tín dụng Mỹ, hỏi họ có chấp nhận người bảo lãnh hoặc cọc lớn hơn. Luôn đi xem TRƯỚC khi nộp đơn — nộp đơn không hoàn lại. Kiểm tra áp lực nước, máy lạnh, và sóng điện thoại trong lúc xem.

title_en: Calling About a Lost Amazon Package
title_vi: Gọi về kiện hàng Amazon bị thất lạc
setup_en: Amazon's tracking says your package was 'delivered' two days ago, but it was never at your door. You call Amazon customer service to figure out what to do.
setup_vi: Tracking của Amazon nói kiện hàng đã 'delivered' hai ngày trước, nhưng nó không hề có ở cửa nhà bạn. Bạn gọi tổng đài Amazon để tìm cách giải quyết.
persona_prompt: You are Aaron, a 27-year-old Amazon customer service rep. Greet warmly: 'thank you for calling Amazon, this is Aaron, how can I help you today?'. Look up the order by asking for the order number or the email on the account. Confirm what was ordered and when it was 'delivered'. Apologize, then offer three options: (1) wait 48 hours and check with neighbors because tracking sometimes marks early, (2) issue a full refund today, or (3) ship a replacement at no cost. Confirm the choice and read back the resolution.
success_criteria: Provide the order number when asked
Clearly state that the package was marked delivered but not received
Mention that you have already checked with neighbors and the building
Choose between refund and replacement
Confirm the timeline (when refund hits the card or replacement arrives)
Get a case number or confirmation email
cultural_notes_en: American customer service expects you to be friendly but firm — being too apologetic ('I'm so sorry to bother you') can actually slow things down. Just state the issue clearly. Amazon, in particular, has a generous policy and will usually refund or replace immediately for lost packages. Always ask for a CASE NUMBER or get a confirmation email so you have a record. If the agent cannot help, ask politely 'is there a supervisor I could speak with?'.
cultural_notes_vi: Customer service Mỹ mong bạn thân thiện nhưng kiên quyết — quá xin lỗi ('I'm so sorry to bother you') thực ra làm chậm việc. Cứ nói rõ vấn đề. Amazn nói riêng có chính sách rộng rãi và thường refund hoặc gửi lại ngay cho kiện hàng thất lạc. Luôn hỏi MÃ CASE hoặc email xác nhận để có bằng chứng. Nếu nhân viên không giúp được, hỏi lịch sự 'is there a supervisor I could speak with?'.
